assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect reshaped how band structure is classified: topology, not symmetry breaking, protects edge and surface states. It is original, conceptually clear, and has become an organizing principle across electronic-structure theory and materials discovery, including first-principles searches for topological materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall effect in graphene). Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization in HgTe/CdTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. A Kane, Mele, Molenkamp trio is a fair configuration, though the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang contribution is not in the supplied credit and would be an allocation concern.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent experiments (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3-class 3D materials) and by a large body of ab initio work; interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions leaving room for this distinct step.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among the Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu-Kane-Mele 3D insulator contributions is not fully resolved by the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 prize may be raised as a concern by some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Current-induced spin-orbit torques allow electrical switching of magnetization without an external polarizer, with direct importance for magnetic memory and for the physics of spin-orbit coupling at interfaces. The work connects relativistic electronic structure, interface magnetism and magnetization dynamics, which I can assess closely.
assessment.attribution: Miron and Gambardella (with colleagues) demonstrated Rashba-type torque switching in Pt/Co/AlOx; Buhrman's group demonstrated spin-Hall torque switching in Pt and Ta/CoFeB. Both lines are distinct but converge on the same discovery, so a three-person split is defensible. Microscopic origin (spin Hall versus interfacial Rashba) was debated and remains partially unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and by industrial development of SOT-MRAM. The physical origin of the torque in specific systems is still partly disputed, so the underlying interpretation is mature in outcome but not fully settled in mechanism.
uncertainties: Relative roles of bulk spin Hall and interfacial Rashba-Edelstein contributions remain contested.
Earlier theory (Dyakonov-Perel, Hirsch, Zhang, Manchon) is not in the supplied credit and could complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moire flat bands in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform for correlated insulators, superconductivity and magnetism in a single clean material. The discovery changed the field of two-dimensional materials and links directly to electronic-structure theory with large unit cells and strong correlations.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered correlated insulators and superconductivity experimentally. Theory plus experiment gives a natural trio. Other contributors (for example Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, and Dean, Kim, Young on hBN-based moire) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely across many groups and device types, though the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated phases is still actively debated. Recognition is plausible now but the field is still young, with some risk of premature timing.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit overlap with earlier moire band theory and with hBN-encapsulation experimental work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Femtosecond demagnetization and all-optical magnetic switching opened ultrafast magnetism and showed that spin order can be manipulated on sub-picosecond timescales. This is close to my own work on atomistic spin dynamics and ultrafast magnetization dynamics, and I recognize its importance and its remaining open questions.
assessment.attribution: Beaurepaire et al. (1996) discovered ultrafast demagnetization in nickel; Kimel, Rasing and colleagues demonstrated inverse Faraday-type optical control of magnetization, and later all-optical helicity-independent switching in GdFeCo with Stanciu and others. Credit between these discoveries is distinct and a trio spanning both is reasonable but leaves out other contributors.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally reproduced widely, but the microscopic mechanisms of ultrafast demagnetization (spin-flip scattering, superdiffusive transport, exchange-driven transfer) are still debated, which weakens the case for a clean, stable interpretation.
uncertainties: No consensus on the mechanism of ultrafast demagnetization.
Credit for all-optical switching may need to include contributors outside the supplied names (for example Stanciu, Hansteen, Tsukamoto).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of iron-pnictide superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx (Tc about 26 K, raised above 50 K) opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors with multiband, magnetism-linked pairing. The importance for correlated-electron physics and for first-principles studies of Fe-based magnetism is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the initial discovery; Chen and Zhao were prominent in rapidly raising Tc with rare-earth substitution. A prize to Hosono alone is fair on priority, with Chen and Zhao as plausible co-recipients, but the supplied names allow one to three laureates.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and the materials class is well established, but the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and applications are limited. Recognition is plausible but not urgent; the discovery is over 15 years old and mature in observation.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism not settled (spin-fluctuation s-plus-minus versus orbital).
Whether Chen and Zhao should share credit with Hosono is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Superconductivity in the (TMTSF)2X Bechgaard salts was the first in an organic conductor and revealed rich physics of quasi-one-dimensional correlated electrons, spin-density waves and unconventional pairing. The conceptual significance is high, especially for correlated electrons, though the later influence is more indirect than for newer platforms.
assessment.attribution: Bechgaard synthesized the compounds and Jérome led the discovery of superconductivity under pressure, so a two-person prize is clean. Other early collaborators (Mazaud, Ribault, Andres, Thorup) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over four decades of independent confirmation and stable interpretation, so very mature; risk is that the field's importance has been overtaken by later correlated-electron systems.
uncertainties: Impact on the wider field is narrower than for other candidates.
Unconventional pairing nature in these salts is still discussed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect, predicted for magnetic topological insulators and observed as a quantized Hall plateau at zero field, is a clear realization of topological transport driven by magnetism and spin-orbit coupling. The prediction used first-principles band calculations, which is close to my methods and shows the power of electronic-structure theory.
assessment.attribution: Dai, Fang and coworkers made the 2010 theoretical proposal and Xue's group produced the 2013 experimental observation in Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3. Haldane's earlier model and independent work by Chang and others, plus Chang's lead role, complicate a clean trio.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in several groups, but the quantization occurs only at very low temperature and the materials are demanding to grow, so applied maturity is limited. Timing is plausible but may be better after further development.
uncertainties: Credit relative to Haldane's 1988 model and other experimental contributors (for example Cui-Zu Chang) is not settled.
Low operating temperature limits practical impact for now.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level, based on Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea, advanced precision measurement and opened tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. They are important metrology, though further from my own field.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and Ye led the demonstration of record precision, giving a two-person configuration. Other ion-clock and lattice-clock contributors (Hall, Hänsch were already honored in 2005, and Wineland in 2012) lie outside the credit supplied.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks now agree at the 10^-18 level, and the technology is mature, though redefinition of the second has not yet occurred. Recognition is timely but not urgent.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion-trap clocks may reduce novelty.
I do not have independent verification of the latest performance figures.
